Taiwan Lifts Temporary Steel Export Restrictions, Industry Operations Resume

TAIPEI, June 12—Taiwan's government has lifted temporary export restrictions on certain steel products, imposed last month amid concerns over domestic supply shortages, industry and government officials said Wednesday. The move has allowed steelmakers, including Kao Hsing Chang Iron & Steel, to resume international shipments after several weeks of limited operations.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs said in a statement that the restrictions, which took effect on May 14, were introduced to "ensure stable domestic supply of hot-rolled coil and related products during a period of heightened construction demand." The measure limited exports of key steel products, including hot-rolled and cold-rolled coils, by capping outbound shipments at 60% of companies’ monthly averages from the previous year.

Steel industry groups had warned the restrictions would impact revenue and disrupt longstanding client relationships overseas. Kao Hsing Chang Iron & Steel, a major producer based in Kaohsiung, reported a 15% decline in export volumes during the period. "We appreciate the government's efforts to balance supply, but the restrictions caused delays and additional costs for us and our partners," said Kao Hsing Chang Iron & Steel spokesperson Lee Wen-cheng. “We are now working to fulfill backlogged overseas orders.”

The Taiwan Steel Producers Association welcomed the lifting of the measure, saying the domestic market had stabilized, making the restrictions unnecessary. “We have seen supply pressures ease in recent weeks, and it is crucial for our industry to maintain its reputation as a reliable exporter,” said association chairperson Chen Yu-fen.

Analysts said the short-term measure highlighted the challenges of balancing domestic needs with export commitments in Taiwan’s steel sector, which exported $5.2 billion worth of products in 2023. "Even brief disruptions can ripple through the supply chain," noted James Ma, a Taipei-based industry consultant. "Restoring normal export flows quickly is key to retaining market share in a competitive global market."

Exports from affected companies, including Kao Hsing Chang Iron & Steel and others, resumed at full capacity this week, officials confirmed.
